extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; statesmen and legal theorists
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria from Hobbes' Leviathan about the nature and proper practice of counsel, exhortation, and the making and promulgation of civil law — i.e., how sovereigns should be advised and how laws obtain authority. Useful for analysing good counsel, deliberative form, and legislative legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Command
rubrics_metrics.description: COMMAND is, where a man saith, 'Doe this,' or 'Doe this not,' without expecting other reason than the Will of him that sayes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands are directed to the commander’s own benefit (the reason of a command is his will). A person may be obliged to obey a command (e.g., by covenant to obey). Commands do not require the commander to supply reasons beyond his will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Counsell
rubrics_metrics.description: COUNSELL, is where a man saith, 'Doe' or 'Doe not this,' and deduceth his own reasons from the benefit that arriveth by it to him to whom he sayes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel is directed to the benefit of the person counselled; it does not (by itself) obligate them. One cannot claim a right to be another's counsellor; asking counsel implies the asker permits whatever counsel is given. Counsel given to induce unlawful action is punishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhortation and Dehortation (Counsel vehemently pressed)
rubrics_metrics.description: EXHORTATION, and DEHORTATION, is Counsell, accompanied with signes in him that giveth it, of vehement desire to have it followed; or, more briefly, Counsell Vehemently Pressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhortation tends to be directed to the speaker’s own benefits and uses rhetorical tools (similitudes, metaphors, appeals to passion). It is appropriate when addressing a multitude or when a leader's encouragement is necessary (father, army leader), but when used as counsel to a sovereign it indicates corrupt counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsellor must have aligned interests (no conflict)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first condition of a good Counsellour: That His Ends, And Interest, Be Not Inconsistent With The Ends And Interest Of Him He Counselleth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsellors whose private ends conflict with the sovereign’s produce suspect or unfaithful advice. Avoid advisors with incompatible incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, firmness, and brevity of counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsell ought to be propounded 'with as firme ratiocination, as significant and proper language, and as briefly, as the evidence will permit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good counsel avoids rash, unevident inferences (e.g., mere appeals to authority or isolated examples), obscure/confused/ambiguous expressions, and metaphoric speech that stirs passions rather than shows consequences. Counsel should make consequences manifest with clear reasoning and proper language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rhetorical devices that obscure reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Rash, And Unevident Inferences; Obscure, Confused, And Ambiguous Expressions; All Metaphoricall Speeches, Tending To The Stirring Up Of Passion, Are Repugnant To The Office Of A Counsellour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oratorical flourishes that inflame passion or favour the speaker’s interest are inappropriate for genuine counsel. Use reasoned argumentation, not emotional rhetoric, when advising on public business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain expertise and experience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No Man Is Presumed To Be A Good Counsellour, But In Such Businesse, As He Hath Not Onely Been Much Versed In, But Hath Also Much Meditated On, And Considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsell depends on experience and long study; one should only advise where one has specialized experience and sustained reflection. The best counsellors are those with practical and contemplative mastery of the relevant subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special competence for foreign affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: To counsel on business that hath reference to another Common-wealth, It Is Necessary To Be Acquainted With The Intelligences, And Letters That Come From Thence, And With All The Records Of Treaties, And Other Transactions Of State Between Them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors on international matters must have access to and familiarity with diplomatic intelligence, treaty records, and prior state transactions; outsiders lacking such knowledge cannot give good counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer private consultation over large assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: Supposing the number of Counsellors equall, a man is better Counselled by hearing them apart, then in an Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing counsellors individually yields fuller, less-conformed advice: prevents eloquence-driven bandwagoning, allows interrogation and testing of reasons, reduces passions amplified by crowds, and preserves secrecy where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangers of large assemblies for counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: In an Assembly of many, passions and eloquence may inflame opinions, some with contrary interests will be present, and members may speak for applause or fear rather than truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large public deliberations risk conformity, passion, secrecy loss, and obstruction of execution. Important or secret state business should be entrusted to smaller, trusted groups of experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on who may give effective counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: They who are not called to Counsell can have no good Counsel in such cases to obtrude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only persons whose experience, office, or appointment fit the matter should intrude advice; unsolicited counsel from the unqualified is unlikely to be valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: On the structure of deliberation and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A man that doth his businesse by the help of many and prudent Counsellours, with every one consulting apart in his proper element, does it best; he that useth his own judgement only does next best; but a framed Counsel that cannot move but by plurality often retards execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberative structures should ensure a single decisive resolution (final resolution in one person) rather than requiring concurrent consent of many; fragmentation of responsibility impedes action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Civil Law
rubrics_metrics.description: CIVILL LAW, Is to every Subject, those Rules, which the Common-wealth hath Commanded him, by Word, Writing, or other sufficient Sign of the Will, to make use of, for the Distinction of Right, and Wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil law is authoritative only when commanded by the sovereign and made known by sufficient signs; laws function to distinguish right from wrong for those obliged to obey.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sovereign as sole Legislator
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislator in all Common-wealths, is only the Soveraign, be he one Man, ... or one Assembly of men, as in a Democracy, or Aristocracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative power resides in the person or body that constitutes the sovereign (the representative). Only the sovereign can make or abrogate laws; subordinate bodies cannot independently possess legislative authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign not subject to civil law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soveraign of a Common-wealth ... is not subject to the Civill Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the sovereign can make and repeal laws, he cannot be bound by them in the same way subjects are; he is 'free' in that he can release himself by repealing laws. (Normative claim about sovereignty's immunity.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom and long use derive authority from sovereign consent, not time
rubrics_metrics.description: When long Use obtaineth the authority of a Law, it is not the Length of Time that maketh the Authority, but the Will of the Soveraign signified by his silence (for Silence is sometimes an argument of Consent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs gain force only insofar as the sovereign tacitly accepts them; prescription by time alone does not create law against the sovereign's will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between Natural Law and Civil Law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law of Nature, and the Civill Law, contain each other, and are of equall extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural law (equity, justice, gratitude) becomes civil law when a commonwealth is instituted (commands of the sovereign). Conversely, civil law is part of the dictates of nature (e.g., fidelity and performance of covenants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provincial/customary laws derive force from present sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: Provinciall Lawes Are Not Made By Custome, But By The Soveraign Power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws observed in provinces are laws by virtue of present sovereign authority, not merely prescription; where unwritten usages are general and reasonable they may be natural law, but otherwise their force rests on the sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law must be made known to be law (promulgation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Law Made, If Not Also Made Known, Is No Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A command is law only to those who have means to take notice of it. Exceptions: laws of nature (universally knowable) need no promulgation. Those incapable of understanding (natural fools, children, madmen) are not bound in the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten obligations for officers default to reason/fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a public minister is employed without written instructions, he is obliged to take for Instructions the Dictates of Reason; all which Instructions of naturall Reason may be comprehended under one name of Fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of written law or instructions, officials must act according to reason and fidelity to the sovereign's interest; unwritten rules binding particular persons are effectively natural-law obligations known by their reasoned condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to be bound by law (promulgation & understanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over naturall fooles, children, or mad-men there is no Law, no more than over brute beasts; nor are they capable of the title of just, or unjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binding force of law presupposes the capacity to understand and make covenants; inability to take notice of particular law excuses noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law's reason is the sovereign's reason/intent
rubrics_metrics.description: That Law can never be against Reason ... the doubt is, of whose Reason it is, that shall be received for Law. It is ... the Reason of this our Artificiall Man the Common-wealth, and his Command, that maketh Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that law must conform to 'reason' are interpreted as conformity to the sovereign's reason/intent; subordinate judges should interpret laws in light of the sovereign's purpose.
